findings.how_to_check: Run `python replication/extract_deaglan_tables.py --check` (or `python replication/extract_deaglan_tables.py --regenerated F:/Deaglan/Census_Transcriptions/output/tables`) before `linkage_table_abe_jw_nontarget.tex` and `linkage_table_hlink_nontarget.tex` have been manually copied into the paper repository's `linkage_tables/` folder.
findings.suggested_fix: In `check_reproduction()`, check `if not committed.exists():` before calling `sha256(committed)` (print `MISSING (committed) {fname}` and set `ok = False`). In `main()`, guard `read(committed)` with `if committed.exists():`; when `committed` does not exist yet but `--regenerated` supplies `regen`, read `rtext, eol = read(regen)` and extract `figures/deaglan_{name}.tex` from `regen` while setting `failed = True` until the reference table is committed to `linkage_tables/`.
findings.title: extract_deaglan_tables.py crashes with FileNotFoundError when newly added tables are not yet in linkage_tables/
findings.what_the_code_does: Commit 067b885 adds `"abe_jw_nontarget"` and `"hlink_nontarget"` to `TABLES` (`ALL_TABLES = TABLES`). In `check_reproduction()`, lines 67-71 check `if not regen.exists():` and then immediately execute `a, b = sha256(regen), sha256(committed)` without checking `committed.exists()`. In `main()`, line 133 executes `ctext, eol = read(committed)` unconditionally at the start of the `for name in TABLES:` loop before the `if args.regenerated:` block (lines 136-146).
findings.why_it_matters: Because `linkage_table_abe_jw_nontarget.tex` and `linkage_table_hlink_nontarget.tex` are new outputs produced by the Machine B Stata run in `$OUT_TABLES`, they do not exist in the paper repository's `linkage_tables/` directory prior to that run, and neither `Run-MachineB.ps1` nor `extract_deaglan_tables.py` copies regenerated tables into `linkage_tables/`. When `Run-MachineB.ps1` completes the ~4-hour Stata run and calls `extract_deaglan_tables.py --paper-repo $paper --regenerated $tables` (or when `extract_deaglan_tables.py` is run on either machine before `linkage_tables/` is manually populated), it crashes with an uncaught `FileNotFoundError` and fails to extract `figures/deaglan_abe_jw_nontarget.tex` and `figures/deaglan_hlink_nontarget.tex`.

findings.how_to_check: Compare `Share validated, MI (%)` (Old: 88.87%, New: 88.21%) against `Share validated, Ancestry 1940 MI (%)` (Old: 88.87%, New: 89.07%) under `## Non-target records` in `MATCHING/results/tgt_linkage_abe.md:50-52`, and compare `MATCHING/score_tgt_links.do:217-223` with `LINKAGE/code/01_abe_jw/linkage_analysis.do:269-280`.
findings.suggested_fix: In `LINKAGE/code/01_abe_jw/linkage_analysis.do:260-280` and `LINKAGE/code/02_hlink/linkage_analysis_newlinks.do:392-412`, also compute fixed-yardstick middle-initial validation using `mi_anc` as the 1940 middle initial for both `Old` and `New` (as done in `MATCHING/score_tgt_links.do:217-223`), display it in the log, and include or report it for the non-target tables so link-set quality changes are separated from 1940 middle-initial re-transcription on non-target records.
findings.title: Non-target MI match rate switches the 1940 middle-initial yardstick between Old and New, reversing the sign of the quality change on ABE links
findings.what_the_code_does: In `PART 2` of both scripts (`linkage_analysis.do:269` `local miv = cond(strpos("`combo'", "_old"), "mi_anc", "mi_ml")` and `linkage_analysis_newlinks.do:401` `local miv = cond("`ver'" == "old", "mi_anc", "mi_ml")`), the non-target sample (`samp == "non"`, `target == 0`) scores `Old` links against Ancestry's 1940 middle initial (`mi_anc`) and `New` links against the model's 1940 middle initial (`mi_ml`). Only this own-initial `MI Match Rate (%)` is computed and written to `linkage_table_abe_jw_nontarget.tex` and `linkage_table_hlink_nontarget.tex`.
findings.why_it_matters: Non-target records (`target == 0`) are defined by Ancestry and FamilySearch agreeing on 1940 first and last name (`!(namefrst==namefrst_fs & namelast==namelast_fs)` in `LINKAGE/code/prep/build_linkage_sample1940.do:52`), not on middle initial, and under a target-only replacement policy (`MATCHING/score_tgt_links.do:106-108`) non-target records retain Ancestry's transcription and `mi_anc`. Switching the 1940 validation initial from `mi_anc` to `mi_ml` on non-target records conflates changes in the linked pair set with differences between model and Ancestry middle-initial transcriptions. On ABE exact non-target links (`MATCHING/results/tgt_linkage_abe.md:50-56`), own-initial MI validation falls from 88.87% (Old) to 88.21% (New), whereas holding the 1940 initial fixed at `mi_anc` shows validation rising from 88.87% to 89.07% (consistent with the contradicted share falling from 4.48% to 4.13%). Because the purpose of the ~4-hour Machine B run (`review/handoff_nontarget_machineB.md:7-16`) is to obtain non-target MI validation rates for JW and HLINK, omitting the fixed-`mi_anc` calculation leaves the run unable to isolate link quality changes on non-target records without another 4-hour rerun.

structured_output.summary: Commit 067b885 cleanly extends the ABE/JW and HLINK linkage analysis scripts to compute Panel A statistics on the 1940 non-target sample (`target == 0`), enforcing exact additive partitioning (`full = restr + non`) across all counts and reconciling the ABE non-target numbers against Machine A's `MATCHING/results/tgt_linkage_abe.md`. However, adding `abe_jw_nontarget` and `hlink_nontarget` to `TABLES` in `replication/extract_deaglan_tables.py` without guarding against missing committed reference files in `linkage_tables/` will cause `extract_deaglan_tables.py` (and `Run-MachineB.ps1`) to crash with `FileNotFoundError` before extracting the newly generated tables. In addition, scoring non-target `Old` vs. `New` links only against each version's own 1940 middle initial (`mi_anc` vs. `mi_ml`) confounds link-set changes with middle-initial transcription differences—which on ABE non-target links reverses the sign of the MI validation change (-0.66 pp own-MI vs. +0.20 pp fixed Ancestry-MI in `MATCHING/results/tgt_linkage_abe.md`).

verified_clean.evidence: In LINKAGE/code/01_abe_jw/linkage_analysis.do:84-96,577-585 and LINKAGE/code/02_hlink/linkage_analysis_newlinks.do:238-250,639-651, `assert inlist(target, 0, 1)` verifies `target` is binary and non-missing before `keep if target == 0`, denominator additivity (`N_men_1940_restr + N_men_1940_non == N_men_1940_full`) is enforced, and Part 5 verifies `full == restr + non` for `N_linked`, `verified`, `unverifiable`, `contradicted`, `FN`, `mi_denom`, and `mi_match` across every method and version.
verified_clean.item: Non-target sample construction and exact full = restr + non count partitioning

verified_clean.evidence: In LINKAGE/code/01_abe_jw/linkage_analysis.do:132-138,250-258 and LINKAGE/code/02_hlink/linkage_analysis_newlinks.do:270-276,382-390, `true_pairs_non` filters `true_pairs_full` to `den1940_non` (uniquely keyed on `histid` via `isid histid` at line 64 / 199). Because sample `non` links are also restricted to `histid1940` in `den1940_non`, true pairs in `true_pairs_non` can only be recovered in `samp == "non"`, so `verified_non + FN_non` equals `_N` of `true_pairs_non` and partitions `true_pairs_full`.

summary.description: Two to four sentences. The overall state of the reviewed work and the single most important thing to fix. No preamble.

dimensions_reviewed.description: Which scope dimensions were actually reviewed in this run.

findings.description: Defects and concerns, ordered most severe first. Empty if none. Do not pad with stylistic observations.

severity.description: blocker: a reported result is wrong. major: a referee would demand it. minor: real but survivable. nit: cosmetic.

confidence.description: verified: traced in the source. likely: strongly implied but depends on unseen data. speculative: a question, not an established defect.

title.description: One line, stating the defect itself, not its category.

location.description: path:line, or path:line-line. Several may be comma-separated. Required: a finding without a location is not a finding.

what_the_code_does.description: Precisely what the code computes, quoting the relevant expression. Contrast with what it was evidently intended to compute.

why_it_matters.description: The consequence for a number or claim in the paper. If there is no consequence, the severity is nit.

how_to_check.description: A concrete command, tabulation, or count the author can run to confirm or refute this in minutes.

suggested_fix.description: The change, specific enough to act on. Do not apply it yourself.

verified_clean.description: Things explicitly checked that were fine. This is what makes a short findings list trustworthy rather than lazy.

evidence.description: How it was confirmed, with path:line where applicable.

review_limits.description: What this review could NOT establish: data not readable, pipeline not runnable, paper text unavailable, Stata semantics not verifiable by reading. Be explicit; silence here reads as false assurance.
